summary: Iter149 frontend role/permission refinement tested. 6/11 test groups PASS, 4 FAIL due to one critical regression: EnforcePortalScope clears single-portal tokens when URL leaves that portal scope, defeating the new AccessDenied flow. AccessDenied page renders on first cross-portal hit, but the safety/hr token is wiped on the same render cycle (useEffect), so the user becomes anonymous immediately — clicking 'Back to <Home Portal>' routes to that portal's login page instead of the hub, and any further cross-portal navigation falls through to the anonymous login redirect (no AccessDenied).

integration_issues.issue: EnforcePortalScope (/app/frontend/src/components/EnforcePortalScope.jsx) clears the single-portal token (clearSafetyToken / clearHrToken / etc.) on the same render cycle in which RequireHr/RequireSafety/etc. renders AccessDenied. The Require* guard sees isSignedInAnywhere()==true on first paint and renders AccessDenied with 'Back to Safety Portal' button — but EnforcePortalScope's useEffect simultaneously clears the safety token because pathname '/hr' is not inScope('/safety-portal'). Result: by the time the user clicks the CTA, the safety token is gone → Navigate guard on /safety-portal bounces to /safety-portal/login. Every subsequent cross-portal navigation by the same user falls through the anonymous branch (Navigate to login, not AccessDenied).

action_items: CRITICAL — Fix the EnforcePortalScope vs AccessDenied conflict. Recommended approach: EnforcePortalScope should NOT clear single-portal tokens when the current route belongs to a DIFFERENT portal namespace (i.e. when the user is bouncing through AccessDenied). Concretely, change the rule from 'clear when not inScope(/safety-portal)' to 'clear when pathname is /, /training/*, or belongs to NO known portal namespace' — i.e. only clear on truly-public surfaces, not on other portals' surfaces. Cross-portal navigation should leave existing portal tokens intact so AccessDenied retains its 'Back to <Home Portal>' affordance.
Alternate fix: have AccessDenied set a one-shot flag (sessionStorage masci.access-denied=1) that EnforcePortalScope skips on. Less clean but localized.
After fix, re-run T5/T6/T7/T10/T11 — all should turn green without re-logging in between.
critical_code_review_comments: The Iter149 implementation is solid (clean AccessDenied page, good testids, sensible permissions.js helpers, correct Hub.jsx split). The miss is purely the EnforcePortalScope interaction — that component existed before Iter149 and was not updated to be AccessDenied-aware. The cleanest fix lives in EnforcePortalScope.jsx, not in the Require* guards.

isSignedInAnywhere() reads from localStorage synchronously, so the first paint of AccessDenied is correct. The bug only manifests on subsequent renders / clicks because EnforcePortalScope's useEffect runs AFTER first paint and silently nukes the token.
/app/frontend/src/pages/Hub.jsx — 'Your Portals' / 'Other Portals' split is correct and matches spec. Anonymous full-grid path is correct.
AccessDenied.jsx — clean, accessible, mobile-friendly. No issues.

rca_of_the_issue: RACE between RequireHr (renders AccessDenied on first paint when isSignedInAnywhere()) and EnforcePortalScope (useEffect after first paint clears masci.safety.token because pathname /hr is not inScope('/safety-portal')). First paint is correct, but the post-paint effect strands the user. Reproduction: 1) Log into Safety. 2) Visit /hr — see AccessDenied with 'Back to Safety Portal'. 3) Open DevTools → Application → Local Storage — observe masci.safety.token has been removed. 4) Click 'Back to Safety Portal' → land on /safety-portal/login because RequireSafety now sees no token. Mitigation: update EnforcePortalScope inScope() rule to treat ALL portal namespaces ('/admin', '/pm', '/shop', '/hr', '/safety-portal', '/dispatch-portal') as 'in scope' for every portal token — i.e. only clear tokens on truly-public surfaces ('/', '/training/*', '/cheatsheet', '/field', '/qaqc', '/safety', '/sign-in', login pages, etc.). Cross-portal traversal must preserve tokens so AccessDenied works as designed.
